prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, in which ligand design makes the construction of aryl amines a predictable catalytic reaction

statement.case_for: Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling remains the candidate where concept, maturity and attribution all hold at once. The new element beyond the 2010 prize is mechanistic: palladium amido intermediates and a hard C-N reductive elimination had to be controlled by ligand design, first with bidentate phosphines and then with bulky electron-rich ligands, and that control is what turned a niche tin-amide reaction into a general method. Three decades of independent use in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis confirm it, and Buchwald and Hartwig worked in parallel and independently, so a two-name prize needs no forced omission. Round 1 did not produce a majority for anything, but no member disputed the science or the pair, and the objections raised (the 2010 overlap, Kosugi) concern framing and wording, which a citation can handle.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize for C-C cross-coupling will make some colleagues read this as a downstream extension, and the committee could reasonably prefer a discovery that opens a new field over a synthetic method. Kosugi's and Migita's tin-amide chemistry is a real precursor that a two-name prize leaves unnamed. Support is also narrow: three preferences in round 1, with B026 close behind, so I cannot claim that this is the committee's broad view.

responses.point: Peter prefers targeted protein degradation (B026) with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and says that B065 would be the safer choice if the PROTAC and glue strands cannot be reconciled.
responses.response: That last sentence is where I think we agree. I accept that B026 is a real change of pharmacological principle, and I rank it as my first alternative. The difficulty is that a trio of Crews, Deshaies and Handa joins two strands that the field itself keeps apart, and Ciulli, Ito and Gray would remain outside. With no approved degrader, I would rather let the clinical record and the attribution mature than fix a trio now that we would have to defend as a compromise. If the committee wanted B026 this year, I would support your Handa version over a PROTAC-only citation, because the glue strand should not be silently dropped.

responses.point: Daniel prefers B026 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli and argues that the VHL and cereblon mechanisms are independently confirmed and that the concept is chemically explicit.
responses.response: I do not dispute the independent confirmation, and the chemistry of linker, ligand and ternary-complex design is explicit. I weigh Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands as a major step, but a Crews-Deshaies-Ciulli trio is a PROTAC prize, and this leaves the cereblon work of Handa and Ito, which gave the mechanistic explanation of the glue strand, uncredited. Your own uncertainty list asks the same question about the third name. I treat it as a sign that the credit structure is not yet settled, whereas for B065 it is settled.

responses.point: Heiner, as chair, narrows B037 to Balasubramanian and Klenerman, a two-name Solexa prize for reversible-terminator sequencing by synthesis on clonal arrays.
responses.response: Narrowing to the pair makes the case clearly stronger than the opening trio, and it moves B037 from a marginal alternative to my second alternative. The chemistry is real. My remaining difficulty is classification and competing routes: 454, Ju's terminator chemistry and the Lynx clonal arrays are not trivial claims, and the 1980 sequencing prize makes me hesitate to read this as a new chemical principle. If the committee settled on the Solexa pair and a citation tied to the terminator chemistry, I could vote for it. I still prefer B065, where nobody has proposed a different pair.

responses.point: Peter prefers B065 with the same pair, argues that the attribution is unusually clean, and raises whether Kosugi and Migita should be credited and whether a second part might be added.
responses.response: We agree on the pair and on maturity. On Kosugi and Migita, I stay with the citation route: the wording 'general' and 'ligand design' states what Buchwald and Hartwig added. I also keep to my round-1 view against pairing B065 with another synthetic-methodology part. Your B033 alternative has diffuse credit among six or seven names, so a second part from that area would weaken the prize.

responses.point: Emma prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B045) with Cullis, Hope and Madden, resting on lipid phase behaviour and pH-dependent charge, and says that this part of the mRNA story was not recognised by the 2023 Medicine prize.
responses.response: The physical-chemical foundation you describe is persuasive, and I ranked B045 fifth at the opening. I still cannot settle the credit between the Vancouver group, the Anderson and Langer lipidoid line and MacLachlan from the record we have, and the 2023 prize makes timing awkward. I do not see it as an alternative for my ballot, but I would not oppose it in a later year if the allocation is resolved.

uncertainties: Whether a majority accepts the argument that C-N coupling is conceptually distinct from the 2010 prize, since the committee has not discussed this beyond the members who prefer B065.
Whether leaving Kosugi and Migita to the citation will be accepted as sufficient.
Whether B026 will be preferred by a majority this year, and in that case whether the third name is Ciulli or Handa; I have not settled on this.
Whether B037, restricted to the Solexa pair, is accepted as chemistry.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has arisen since round 1, and none applies to B065. My connections to Arieh Warshel and the Uppsala ribosome and RNA community involve no shortlisted candidate. B032 (energy landscapes) is close to my field and is not in my configuration; I would flag it again if it became a serious contender.
